sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report defines two populations of interest: ECEC centres at ISCED level 02 and ECEC centres for children under three years (U3). Sampling is implemented as a first-stage random sample of 180 centres followed by a second-stage random sample of 8 staff per selected centre when possible. Home-based settings are part of the international target population but are excluded by all participating countries for ISCED level 02 coverage, and some countries also exclude home-based settings for the U3 population. The report further defines participation criteria for adjudication (e.g., a centre is participating for centre/centre leader data if the leader returned at least one valid response; for staff data, at least 50% of selected staff must return questionnaires).

data.outcome_summary: TALIS Starting Strong 2018 is a technical report describing how the OECD/IEA TALIS Starting Strong survey was designed and implemented to produce robust international indicators on ECEC centre staff and centre leaders, including their pedagogical and professional practices and the learning and well-being environments in centres. The survey covers two populations of interest: ISCED level 02 ECEC centres (typically ages 3 to entry into primary education) and U3 centres (children under three). Data collection occurred in three phases (pilot, field trial, main survey), with rotated questionnaire designs and built-in experiments during the field trial to test question formats and wording. The report specifies a two-stage sampling approach (centres, then staff within centres), excludes home-based settings from ISCED level 02 coverage, and uses weighted estimation for international reporting with Fay’s variant of balanced repeated replication (BRR) for standard errors. Complex scaling is conducted using multiple-group confirmatory factor analysis with measurement invariance testing to support cross-country comparability of scale scores.
